A batch name doubles as the tag value and the bundle key, so it stays
in [A-Za-z0-9_] and unique.

The combined input as row references only: no tagging and no row
copies here, so the page holds one resident copy of the data. The
tag column (when named) is applied inside the worker, and in
rawFor() for the identity tabs that never visit it (the tag wins
over an incoming column of the same name; distinguishing dumps is
its whole point).
The batches that are rows to transform; a reference batch is a $ref.

Rows leave here bound for a worker postMessage, and a structured
clone throws on Alpine's reactive proxies, so unwrap at the source:
the raw stored array holds the plain row objects.

---- inspection scopes ----------------------------------------------
A scope names what Data and Profile speak about for the active tab:
"__all" is the combined stack, anything else a single batch. Options
come from the datasets, or (for an output-only bundle rehydrated
without source) from the keys the outputs themselves carry.

Change the inspection scope. A scope the last Run did not target
computes on demand (all tabs at once, so tab switching stays
instant), then mirrors into the display fields.
scope changed the rows under the pane
Mirror the active scope's out onto each tab's display fields.
Replace everything with one batch (a first paste, a host loadRows).
Append a batch (a later paste, + data, loadRows with append).
The name is a tag value and a bundle key, so outputs are stale.

Any change to the input side: restack, reset every tab to unrun, show
the input in the viewer, tell the host.

In separate mode the views show one batch's output per tab; mirror the
picked batch's out onto the tab's display fields.

A literal identity tab never visits the worker: its output IS the
input, so it displays by reference (tagged copies only when a tag
column asks for them) instead of round-tripping the whole dataset.
Run targets the mode's scopes: the combined stack, or every batch.

A changed fn invalidates every scope it was ever computed for,
lazy ones included.

The bundle (fn/data gzips, src capture) is stale now; it
rebuilds lazily from its pane, a copy, or a download, and
eagerly only while the pane is open watching it.

Compute one scope's outputs for the given tab indexes: identity tabs
resolve by reference (tagged copies only under a tag column), the
rest go through a throwaway worker whose input is the scope's
batches. Used by Run for its targets and by the scope picker for
on-demand scopes.

EVERY BATCH IS A $name, offered only to a run whose fns name it.
It used to take a per-chip switch, which also kept the batch out of
the inputs; now any batch is readable as $name while it is also
transformed, and only a host's reference batch (loadRows with ref)
stays out of the inputs. Seeded by need, since the seed is cloned
to the worker on every run and a workbook can be many sheets.

Materialize the export side on demand: per-batch src gzips, each
ran tab's fn and data gzips, then the bundle string.

The bundle carries the mode's target scopes only ("__all" combined,
else the batches); scopes computed for inspection alone stay out.

A target scope the user never Ran (they inspected a batch chip
and came straight here) computes now; without this the bundle
would emit only meta.

The columnar form exists only here, transiently, one output at a
time: stringify, gzip, release.

Every key the bundle COULD carry, in emit order. rebuildBundle and
the pane's checklist read the same plan, so they cannot disagree.
One auto-named batch keeps the legacy bare `src` key (srcKeyOf);
anything more writes src_<batch>, so boundaries survive round-trip.

meta is the one non-gz key: plain JSON, additive, ignored by older
parsers, and what makes combine/tagCol/batch names/dims round-trip.

---- views ----
The export payload is produced on demand (a click), never held in
state or a DOM attribute, and it follows the format on screen: the
Table mode copies and downloads CSV, the Raw and Editor modes JSON,
the Bundle view its manifest. Always the active tab's OUTPUT rows;
for the identity tab that is, by definition, the (tagged) input.

The bundle panel's checklist: every possible key with its selection
state and built size (blank until its gzip exists). meta rides
whenever it is produced and is not electable.

---- the lower pane: Overview, Dimensions, Bundle ----
One tab shows at a time, and only it works: Dimensions scans while it
shows and Bundle builds while it shows, so a large paste is not
gzipped into a bundle nobody opened. A tap on the tab showing folds
the pane.

The Overview tab: what the workbench holds, as two lists. Each input
with its size and whether it is a reference a fn reads by $name;
each fn with what its last run made in the scope on screen, or why
it has nothing, and the $names it reads.

The pane's own preview: the actual bundle JSON, capped as a preview;
Copy and Download carry it all.

Decoupled viewer dispatch (the tfViewer mounted in the markup below).
Rows travel by reference (the viewer's Table and Tree modes use them
directly); the string payload is only what the Raw mode shows, so it
is a capped preview, never a serialization of the whole dataset.
What a Data or Profile grid shows: one tab's output for one batch.

any normal sync reclaims the viewer
Profile and Pivot compute through kits/table-stats.js. Fetched at
load, so it is normally here; if a view is asked for first, the
view draws when the kit arrives rather than failing.

Rescan only when the rows underneath actually changed; a dimension
toggle calls pvDraw() directly and must not re-derive the defaults
out from under the reader's choice.

One row per column of the data, so the Profile is a grid like any
other: sortable, filterable, copyable, with the column menu. The
figures are TableStats.profile's, the same the viewer's explorer
draws: a type read from the values (a CSV's "$1,234.50" is numeric,
not a string), how full the column is, its distincts, and either
its range or its commonest values.

A column of unique values counts 1 for each, so its counts say
nothing and are left off, as the explorer's Columns view does.

---- Pivot: group by N columns, aggregate one measure ---------------

The two hard halves of a pivot over an arbitrary extract were already
in this file, built from opposite ends and never joined. The dimension
wizard (wizScan, above) discovers which columns determine which, and
profile() types every column and counts its distincts. What was
missing was the middle: group, aggregate, nest. That is this, and it
is short because neither end had to be invented.

What it emits is a {label, note, value, children} tree, the shape the
estate's report format already flattens (web-tools docs/CONVERSATION.md
calls a link to it 📊). So a consumer can draw the same result as an
indented table, a treemap or a till receipt, and this code holds no
opinion about any of them. The flat rows below are for THIS pane's
viewer and its CSV download, and they are a different shape on
purpose: one column per dimension level, which is what a table wants
and what an indented single-label column cannot give.

Sorting is by the aggregate, descending, at every level.

The arithmetic is kits/table-stats.js's (TableStats.pivot), shared
with the viewer's explorer since 2026-10-24: the number parser, the
scan, the defaults, the tree and the flat rows. What stays here is
the pane's state and its drawing.

Drag targets. pvDropAt(i) places the dragged chip at index i of the
dims (a pool chip is added there, a chosen chip is moved there);
pvDropOut removes a chosen chip dropped back on the pool.
pvDropCol(i) is the same gesture onto the Columns container: the
chip leaves the rows if it was there. Two column dimensions at most,
since every key becomes a column.

The pivot as a function of the rows: the same partition as pvTree and
pvFlat, written out self-contained so it can be a recipe tab, chain
through $refs, or be committed as a module with no dependency on
this component. pvFnCfg is the short form the strip shows.
Hand a draft to the host: the pivot as a recipe, or the active tab.

---- Layout: the partition, printed -----------------------------

This view adds no configuration of its own. The dimension chips above
are the whole control surface, and this is a second reading of what
pvTree already built, which is what pvDraw's own note invites: it
computes the partition, the host decides how to draw it.

Two column dimensions make a band over a period, which is the
shape a version-by-year compare wants. One makes a flat header.

The pane reads ONE shape in every mode, which is the flat rows, and
copy and download follow the viewer's mode exactly as Data and
Profile do. Showing the tree in Raw while the table showed rows was
the first cut and it was a trap: what you copy would not have been
what you were looking at. The tree stays reachable where its actual
consumer is, on the component (`__workbench.pvOut.res.tree`), which
is the whole integration point: this computes the partition, the
host decides whether to draw it as an indented table, a treemap or
a till receipt.

---- the markup (a string; hosts drop it into the DOM before Alpine walks,
or Alpine.initTree it after). dataExpr rides verbatim inside the x-data
attribute, so single quotes only.

CONTROLS: how the inputs combine and run, on a row of their own.
Until 2026-10-23 these shared one wrapping row with the batch chips,
and a nine-sheet workbook put Run and Clear in the middle of the
sheet names. No row count here: it was the sum over every batch,
which describes no one table once batches are kept apart; a
batch's size is in its chip's peek.

Live run progress, fed by the worker per function (and per batch
in separate mode).

Clear all: every input, reference, fn tab and output, back to an
empty workbench, on one tap; a paste puts the rows back.

DATA INPUTS: the batch chips and nothing else, one row that scrolls
sideways rather than wrapping, so a workbook's sheets read as a list
of inputs and the functions on the left and the output on the right
keep their places below it.

The batch chips double as the scope selector: click selects what
Data and Profile speak about (computed on demand if the last Run
did not target it), double-click renames in place (the name is the
tag value and the bundle key). The Combined chip leads when there
is more than one batch. A chip is its name and nothing else: its
size is in its peek, the house hover card, which heads the
batch's rows as CSV with its row and column counts. Every batch
is a $name to the fns without asking (the run seeds it), which is why
there is no per-chip $ switch.

The join wrapper carries the border but no radius of its own, so it
takes the btn radius explicitly and overflow-hidden clips both
segments to it; the remove segment follows the selection color, so
a selected chip is one solid unit rather than a dark half against
a white x inside a square outline.

An output-only bundle (rehydrated without source) has no batch
chips; its scopes come from the outputs themselves.

The paste/drop target: a drop zone only while empty. Once a table is
loaded it collapses and the row count moves up beside the controls,
so it stops taking a full row it does not need.
The fn column: the editor, the column's whole height.

The output column: the viewer on top, the lower pane below it
(Overview, Dimensions, Bundle; collapsible, drag-splittable).

The scope readout: which batch (or Combined) the batch
chips up top have selected; the chips are the control.

The three output modes, icon-only. The labels went on
2026-09-14 because this strip shares one row with the
Data/Profile/Pivot tabs, the batch readout and the two
export buttons, and it was the widest thing on the row
that was not naming anything the row did not already
imply. Each carries a note in place of the label, which
is the house rule for a popup (kits/title-tip.js); the icons
are the same three, at the same sizes, so the control is
recognisable at a glance by anyone who knew it wide.
data-title-tip-bare drops the kit's dotted underline, which a
button should not be wearing.

A note here NAMES the destination and does not describe
it: at two or three words it reads in the time a pointer
rests, and nothing in the strip needs a sentence. The
middle one says "JSON tree" rather than anything about
editing, because vanilla-jsoneditor is mounted editable
over a structuredClone and nothing reads the clone back:
typing into it changes the widget and not the rows, so a
note promising an editor would be promising a write path
that does not exist. Renaming it is the honest half of
that; whether the panel should be read-only, or should
write back, is a separate question.

The export text is produced at click time, never bound
into the attribute: with large batches that binding held
the whole dataset in the DOM.

The pivot controls, a second header row under the view
buttons. Group-by chips carry their nesting position as a
number, because the order is the whole of what distinguishes
one pivot from another and a set of on/off chips cannot say
it. A numeric column is offered as a measure; every column is
offered as a dimension, since grouping by a number is a normal
thing to want.

Two containers. "Group by" holds the chosen dimensions in
nesting order; the pool holds the rest. A chip drags within
the first to reorder, from the pool into it to add, and out
of it back to the pool to remove; a tap still toggles, so a
phone gets the same reach without dragging. Native HTML
drag-and-drop, no dependency.

The column axis. A chip here spreads its values across the
table as columns (a crosstab), two deep at most; the total
column stays last. Drag in from the pool or from Group by;
tap or drag out to remove.

Two honesty readouts, both of which stay quiet when there is
nothing to say. A non-additive aggregate means a parent is
NOT the sum of its children, and a reader looking at an
indented column will assume it is unless told.

The pivot as a function: what the chips above mean, written
out. Copy takes the self-contained source (pvFnSrc), which
runs as a tab anywhere; Save hands it to the host as a recipe.

While a dim preview holds the output side, its banner IS the
header: the normal Data/Profile controls hide, the report and
dim-table views switch here, and closing (or any tab, view,
or scope change) reclaims the pane.

Stacked OVER the viewer rather than swapping with it: the three
older views keep their element mounted, so nothing here can
change how Tabulator measures itself.

The lower pane: Overview (what the workbench holds), Dimensions (the
active fn's output read for keys and the dimension tables they
define) and Bundle (the export), one at a time. Each tab's readout
and controls sit at the right of the strip.

Dimensions: the live shape of the active tab's output, recomputed
on render so it cannot go stale the way a scan stamp could; the
fact-tab switch, the scan window and a rescan.
Bundle: its size, copy and download, whether or not it is open.

Overview: the inputs and the fns, each a row that selects it, with
the counts in the headers and one line on what outlasts a reload.

The column sidebar: the whole table at a glance (name + distinct
count) and the selection surface in one. Tap once to include a
column (dark), twice to make it a key (blue); several keys form
a compound key, none makes a plain distinct table. Selecting a
candidate paints its columns here.

Acting on the pick: pinned below the list, never scrolled
away. Preview shows it in the viewer, + dim adds the tab,
+ menu lists it with its computed closure, clear starts over.

The rollup tree: a child is a coarser level its parent's key
already delineates; a starred row is a promoted pick. Tap a
row to paint it onto the sidebar.

The selected entry offers what it COULD delineate (lower
cardinality, not carried): tap to fold a column into the
pick, then preview to see where the multiplicities sit.

The checklist: membership is chosen key by key; an unchecked row
stays listed (grayed) so it is one tap to bring back.

:disabled TAKES !! for the same reason the FAB's layer strip
does. bundleRows() stamps a fixed flag on the meta row alone, so
on every real key row the expression was undefined, which Alpine's
x-bind turns into '' for any dotted expression, and '' is not a
value bind() treats as absent: the attribute went on and the
whole checklist was unclickable.

alpineComponents/user-call-form.js — one user call as a form.

A user call is one decision a session needs from the owner (user-call/1,
written by web-tools-private user-calls/user-call.py, one file per call at
user-calls/<session>-<slug>.json
in the repo it governs). This is its form, and it is shaped like the branch
page for the same reason the session page is: a head that says what this is,
over a pane of files to move through.

  Top      what an executive would be shown: the question, one line of
           what is at stake, live facts for a linked PR, and two answers:
           Take, the session's recommendation, or Adjust it. Taking sends
           from the card; an adjustment is written on its own slide below
           (the note, and whether the session goes ahead or comes back
           with a new call), so the card has no note row. A call filed
           before Take and Adjust keeps its options as buttons and its
           note row. A merge is approved, and a documentation call
           recorded, from the verdict circle instead.
           A call that names a decision tree (`tree`) shows where it sits
           in place of its question and brief: the goal at the root and the
           decisions under it, each under the decision it serves, open or
           closed, with its inquiry and instrument as attribute lines, and
           the call's own decision ringed (see loadTree). A second tab, a
           swipe away, says the question plainly: the call's question and
           brief as text. A tree that cannot be read gives the question and
           brief back. A call that names a glossary (`glossary`:
           owner/repo@ref:file.json, entities written by a reader other than
           the call's author) marks each entity's first mention in the
           question, the brief and the tree with a small raised dot.
           Everything the card points to is in the deck below, and the card
           is how a reader gets there: a marked term brings up the Notes
           slide with its note marked, Take brings up what it approves and
           Adjust its form, and a block a material is filed against carries
           a link to it. The top is the decision; the bottom is what
           supports it.
  Bottom   one slide at a time in a snap swiper, as branch-brief's Files
           pane swipes. The Notes, where the call has a tree or a
           glossary: for each entity the question a reader has at its mark
           and the answer, with a ↗ where
           the word's meaning lives elsewhere. One place for every note, so a
           term met twice shows the same note, and nothing floats over the
           text it explains. Then a slide per answer that names one (a
           material's `answer`), then the rest of the materials: a page
           rendered, a document as prose, anything else a button out. In a
           Take or Adjust call, what taking approves leads, before the
           Notes, and the Adjust form ends the deck while the call is open.
           n/m, arrows, and a contents list off the mark, because a swipe
           that starts on a framed page goes to the page.

A DOCUMENTATION CALL IS ANSWERED HERE TOO (owner, 2026-10-29: "It should
just be the call, and that's the form", not Dictate's machinery). The form
reads the call's document where kits/call-answer.js's source() finds its
edits to stage (at the call's base once they are committed, as doc-craft
asks), and draws each one as md-diff's inline reading with its reason, Keep,
Discard and a note. Recording writes the same answer line the Map's Docs tab
writes, with the patch a session applies (answerPatch).

Mounted two ways, as branch-brief is: as a slide in the session page's deck
of calls, and on its own at pages/user-call.html. A host passes:
  call      the envelope, already read (the deck has it)
  src       owner/repo[@ref]:user-calls/<id>.json, read here when `call` is absent
  repo, ref, path   where the call lives, for the answers file beside it
  onAnswer  (entry) => void, told when an answer is sent

Answers go to <id>.answers.jsonl beside the call, one JSON line each,
appended through the owner's token and never edited; the latest line wins.
Where the call names a PR and the box is ticked, the answer is first
commented there, which wakes a session subscribed to it.

window.UserCallForm carries the helpers the session page shares: linkOf (a typed
link to what the renderer draws), prFacts, postAnswer, prOf.

A proof's pill in the colour of what it opens: a view of the app, a
page, a document, or source. The same tints as PR_TONE.

The kind of a shipped change, after Keep a Changelog's verbs plus one
for work that records rather than alters. The glyph leads the line; its
name is the hover title. A line with no kind keeps the plain check.

A tinted disc with dark ink: this theme's success and warning are pale
enough that a bare glyph in them all but disappears.

A page or a document, in the shape a peek or a slide draws; a document's
prose is fetched once, on first use, and kept.
`kind` is md, html, or text: source shown as wrapped text, since a file
named as proof may be a script.

One typed link ({kind, ref, label?}) to where it goes, its mark, and for a
page or a document, the peek.

A PR or a branch opens as the branch page, its guide and files, framed
in the materials pane; GitHub is the mark beside the name. Without a
peek the slide held only a button out to GitHub (owner, 2026-11-03).

A page is its render, a document its prose, anything else its
source as wrapped text.

A tracker task the call decides, owner/repo[@ref]:<path>/tracker/tasks/<id>.md.
Named by its id, the way the Tending view names a task subject; the
task names the call back with `awaiting: user-call <id>`.

A view of the Web Tools app, framed live: ref is the app's own query
(view=map&tab=context). The frame runs the app at this page's ?use=,
chrome off, so the proof is the display the claim is about.

The PR's state, CI on its head, mergeability and size. Read when a form
opens and never written, so never stale.

Append one answer line; comment it on a PR first when asked, so the
comment's address rides in the line. Read fresh, PUT with the sha, and on
a lost race read again, as kits/notes.js appends.
`token` is for a host that keeps its token somewhere other than
window.TOKEN (Dictate reads the stored one); otherwise that global is used.

Branches as branch-brief slides in a deck over whatever is showing: the
session page's branch chips and a call's PR panel both open this. Each
item: { slug, branch, pr?, prState?, icon?, repoShort?, short?, url? }.

`opts.pane` opens every slide on that pane of the branch form ('files'
or 'guide'), for a caller that came for the files rather than the brief.
A document's prose, the same in the pane and in the full-screen deck.

── Step art ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
The tree's steps by their kind, drawn here rather than as icon-font
glyphs: each two-tone in its kind's colour (--k reaches them as
currentColor), with one red detail each, and the goal a filled badge with
a dart in its red bull, so it reads first. The red is the owner's ask: a
little more exciting, not gaudy. Each draws its kind and nothing of one
call's content: the first designs drew the instrument as a key because
that call's was an answer key, which the owner caught.
the fork, its junction lit: where the choice is made, not which way
a closed fork: the path taken solid, the other faded, nothing red
how we tell: a gauge, its needle red

What an adjustment sets off: the session goes ahead, or drafts the change
and puts it back to the owner as a new call (user-call.py, `then`).

The two who talk the question down: Pip, round and curious, and Pap, square
and unimpressed. Drawn in the theme's info and warning colours, paled.

Two cards on the page's own ground, as branch-brief lays out its
guide and its Files pane: the framing above, the materials below.

A DOCUMENTATION CALL IS ONE DOCUMENT, so it takes the slide whole
(owner, 2026-11-07): no ground, no card border, no gap. The two
cards are for the kinds that hold materials beside the question.

AN EXECUTIVE'S GLANCE: the question, one line of what is at
stake, and answers that are only answers. Depth is in the
materials below, never in the answers.

A MERGE CALL is a standard confirm panel, not a question: its
kind and PR, one status line, the verdict circle top right,
then what shipped. Inside the session page's deck the kind,
the PR pill and the circle ride in the deck's header (onHead),
so the card starts at the status; on its own page they lead.
One status line: loose ends and readiness together.

The verdict circle: in the deck's header when hosted,
here, top right, on the call's own page.

The PR as one compact chip in its state's colour, as the
session page draws a branch; its facts speak only when they
are a reason not to answer yet.

The scroll sits one level in: a grid item that scrolls has an
automatic minimum height of zero, so a card at its max height
squeezed it and clipped the open block. A plain item keeps its
content's height, and the card scrolls instead.

TWO WAYS INTO THE QUESTION, a tab each and a swipe between them:
the diagram, and the question said plainly (the call's question and
brief, as text at the card's full width). Each view is one track
wide, and the strip is as tall as the taller, so switching never
moves what is below; it scrolls sideways and the tabs follow it.

The tabs scroll sideways when they outrun a phone. The views
keep one fixed height, each scrolling inside it, so a long
view never pushes the answers down.
Questions anyone would ask, each answered short.
A radio opener: the question as a host would sell it.
Pip and Pap, talking the question down to size.

A documentation call shows no PR readiness (owner, 2026-11-07):
the call asks about wording, and the PR's state is the
session's to settle before it merges.

A documentation call's summary is its brief and each edit's
background and proposal; it shows no recommendation (owner,
2026-11-07).

A DOCUMENTATION CALL is answered here, on the document itself:
md-diff draws the file with each edit as a container that
swipes between the old text, both, and the new, and Keep,
Discard and Note sit on the container. The question, the
brief and the head above the document stay in view, and only
the document scrolls (owner, 2026-11-03): the head names the
file, counts the decisions and links the file's diff on the
call's PR. Record sends one line for the whole call once
every edit is decided, from a row held under the document.

In the deck the header names the file and the list counts the
edits (owner, 2026-11-07), so the line keeps only what neither
says: where the file was read, on its own page, and that a
new document is new.

THE EDITS, LISTED (owner, 2026-11-07): one row per edit with its
short summary, its proposal or else its why; a tap scrolls the
document to that edit, and the row of the edit in view is
marked. A new document has none.
Only Changes draws the edits, so only Changes lists them.

WHAT THE EDIT IS FOR, then its number, then its summary, in
one run of text (owner, 2026-11-08): a flag for a
correction, a wrench for a clarification, from its notes'
kinds (user-call.py), corrections first; then the number,
bold, green once kept and red once discarded. The icon's
name is a title-tip a mouse gets on hover; on a phone a tap
on the row only jumps (data-title-tip-tap).

SELECTION IS AN OUTLINE, AND THE REST STEPS BACK (owner,
2026-11-10): md-diff marks the selected container
(data-md-diff-here) with a wash; here the wash is off,
since a background over md-diff's own marks hurt
legibility, and the container gets a primary outline, a
lighter one under the mouse, while the rest dims.

A PICK CALL is answered on its image board, and its picks
come back beside the call.

THE ANSWERS, in plain view, for a decision: a tap picks one and
a second tap lets it go. Take carries the recommendation and
sends from here; Adjust brings up its form below, which sends
from there. Once answered, the answer that stands stays lit
and the other steps back. An older call's options keep their
star and send from the note row. A merge is approved from its
circle and a documentation call from its edits, so
neither has this row.

On a phone the chip is its glyph alone and gives way to Send,
so the answers keep one line; it wraps below them before the
recommendation is cut.

What is typed here rides with the picked answer. The input
leads at a width it keeps from sm up, so "Post on", the PR chip
and Send sit beside it rather than at the far edge. Where the
tree stands in for the question, the chip names the PR the
answer posts on, and it stays once the call is answered. One
line at a phone's width: the input gives up room, and "Post on"
drops its words below 22rem.

The merge's detail, after the answer rather than before it:
what shipped, and what changes once it is on main.

Each shipped line with its proof: the chip swipes the pane
below to the file or page that shows it, named in a pill.

A head row, the topic in bold and its proof beside it,
then the detail: scanned by the heads, read below. The
leading glyph is the kind of change (CHANGE_KIND), and the
kind decides the detail's shape: Old and New for a change
or a fix, New alone for an addition or a record, Old
alone for a removal.

Old and New as small badges, one width so the text
behind them lines up.

Not merging is not a button: it is a message. Whatever is
typed here goes to the session, posted on the PR, and the
PR stays open.

The verdict menu, dropped from the circle: the call's answers
as rows, the recommended one marked. Picking one sends it.

The PR's panel, the one the session page drops from a branch

Whether the tree stands in for the question and brief: a call with a

── Other ways into the question ──────────────────────────────────
A call may name a views file (`views`: owner/repo@ref:file.json) that

A slide named by an answer, a material's label, or Notes.

What Pip and Pap say about the slide showing, one line at a time.

── The decision tree ─────────────────────────────────────────────
A call names a tree (`tree`: owner/repo@ref:file.json), drawn once the
call and its glossary are read (owner, 2026-10-17). Decisions are the nodes: the goal at the
root, and each decision under the decision it serves, open or closed.
A decision's inquiry (what it waits to know) is an attribute of it, and
the inquiry's instrument (how we find out) an attribute of the inquiry,
since it is the inquiry it answers: plain lines under the pill, the
instrument a step in from its inquiry, never parents of another
decision, so the tree has one link, "serves".
A closed decision shows the path not taken. The call's own decision,
the one whose `call` is this call's id, is ringed. A material whose
`field` names a node (`two-steps`) or an attribute (`two-steps.inquiry`)
hangs a link on that line.
The icon in its kind's colour (--k), its hit area 8px past it.

A decision's body: its attribute lines, then the decisions that serve
it, each joined by a branch; the line down the left runs to the last.
A line of the call's own text, escaped, with its entities marked.

How a marked term looks: a small accent dot raised after it, drawn as the
span's ::after so the term's text stays its own. A bullet character, not a
box: a box after a word is a place the line may break, which on a phone left
the dot at the start of the next line. Never the question-mark
cursor (house style rule 10). A pale wash was tried and rejected, and the
owner never liked the dotted underline; footnote numerals read as powers
beside a call's scores, tinted ink as a link, semibold as emphasis.
Focusable, so a keyboard reaches its note too.

mention of it, here and in the slide, and marks its note; a click or a

else in the card clears it. A touch is read only as its click, since it
sends its pointer out the moment the finger lifts.
Searched from the component's root: called from a handler, $el would be its element.

The note in view on its slide, scrolled within the slide alone, so the

Clear of the slide's foot too, where the app's floating button sits.

One animation at a time: when the strip has to move, the note is
scrolled into view only once it has arrived, since a second smooth

the strip short of its stop on iOS.

A click on the slide: a note pins itself, and a marked term inside one
(the brief's) pins its own note.

Keyboard focus only: a tap focuses the term before its click, and acting on

A click in the card: a block's link brings up its material, a marked term

Back and forward through the notes in the slide's order. A step pins the

The question's views: a tab scrolls the strip to its view, and a

A material by the ref it was filed with, wherever the deck has put it.
A glossary link is a URL or owner/repo@ref:path, which opens on GitHub.
What the ↗ names: a pull request by number, a file by its name.
A proof opens in the materials pane, never away from the page.
Only what would change the answer: a failing check or a conflict.

THE NOTES TAKE THEM OTHERWISE, while the pointer or focus is in the

have clicked: a neighbour loading beside the Adjust form took the

The strip's Left and Right, by the kit's rule for an embedded strip.

The strips' kit. Once it is here both strips land on their slide
and the materials strip takes the arrows (wireKeys).

A host that frames calls in a deck is handed the call's kind and a

Only the number: the header is narrow, and the panel it opens

The kind is the icon's to say; the title is the document, or the

A decision's answers are buttons in the card, and a documentation

A merge's and a documentation call's; a decision's answers are

── Full screen ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
The materials as a deck of their own, over whatever deck holds this
form (drill), or over the page when none does: the house pattern
for looking at one more thing and coming back.
Drilled, the parent's title (the call's kind) is prefixed for us.

A pick call's board, at the version this page runs at, as Waiting
and the session page link it; and the latest picks sent from it.

── A documentation call's edits ──────────────────────────────────
Staged against the file as the call names it, as the Docs tab stages

A CLOSED CALL IS DRAWN FROM ITS OWN EDITS, not the file. Once the

Each edit's old text is a passage, with a rule between passages,
and the decisions are the latest answer's, if it recorded any.

A call filed after its edits were committed, as doc-craft asks,
is decided on the text they replace, at its base (CallAnswer.source).

The document, drawn once it and its host are both here. Each md-diff
change is matched to the call edit whose text it holds; a change no

A row's summary: the edit's proposal, else its why, else the text it puts in.
An edit's kinds from its notes, each once, corrections first.

Where edit i is drawn: its container in Changes, or its line under
the document when the file could not place it.

A row's number: tinted in its decision's hue, so the list reads as a

2026-11-10).

A border, not a ring: the row's text is line-clamped, which hides
overflow, so a ring drawn outside the chip came out clipped.

SELECT IT IN md-diff (md-diff:here), so a tap on a row shows on the

The smooth scroll passes other edits on its way; the spy rests
until it lands, so the marked row does not flicker through them.

The other views draw no containers: go back to Changes, then scroll
once md-diff has drawn them.

The edit in view: the first whose container still shows below the
top of the scrolling document.

DIFF is the whole file as one unified diff with every edit in it,

tab does. A view chosen while it loads wins over it.

md-diff's containers from the view before are cleared first,
or the diff lands under them, out of sight.

OLD AND NEW are the whole file as it stands and with every edit
in it, drawn as md-diff draws an unchanged document; CHANGES is
the file with each edit as a container to decide.

An edit's background and proposal marks, a book and a bulb, are
kits/call-marks.js's, which docPaint draws.

Either way round: a block-sized edit holds its change, and a
section-sized edit is drawn by md-diff as several changes, each
inside the edit's text, all answered by the one decision.

md-diff's jump and layout controls go in the head, so the
document has one sticky band rather than two stacked.

The edit md-diff has selected, by a tap on its container, the
keys, or a row of the list (docJump), so its row and its mark say so.

Each edit's decision stays on its container, as a mark at its top
right, whether or not the container is selected. An edit md-diff
draws as several containers is named once, on its first, which
also carries its reason as a title-tip; the rest show only the

In the place of md-diff's own index, as the Docs tab does, clear
of the reading tabs at the top right.

Room above the container for its label, which sits on its top
edge, when a row of the list scrolls the edit to the top.

BACKGROUND, a book on the edit's name opening its text; the
proposal is the edit's row in the list, under a bulb (owner,
2026-11-07). An edit without a background keeps its why as the tip.

A mouse opens the tip by hovering; leaving the mark, or the
tip after crossing to it, closes it.

An edit's background or proposal: the text alone in a tip under its
name, the book or bulb tapped being its label. Nothing in it is
tappable, so it is a title-tip by the house rule: no ✕, and a tap on
it, a tap elsewhere, Escape or a second tap on its mark closes it.
The text may carry **bold** and `code`; a date stays on one line.
A tap on the mark of the tip on screen closes it; a hover opened it.

A NOTE IS THE CONTAINER'S LAST LINE, typed in place under a dashed
rule, so the document below does not jump and a note stays beside

The call's file read with the address grammar every page boots
(kits/repo-address.js), not CallAnswer, which may still be loading.

A NEW DOCUMENT has no edits to decide (user-call.py's `new`): Record
